scenarios.answer: The module is **`ekos-common::redaction`** (implemented in `ekos/crates/common/src/redaction.rs`), introduced by **RFC 0043 — Global Secrets/PII Redaction**. Its `redact` function replaces every match of every built-in pattern, plus every valid `config.extra_patterns` regex, with `[REDACTED:<label>]`. Per RFC 0043 §5, the redaction is applied right after `let mut package = observer.scan(&ctx).await?;`, before either the artifact-write loop or the `KirObject`-property loop reads `package.artifacts` — so content is already past RFC 0043 redaction before it reaches the artifact store or ledger.

scenarios.answer: No. The `[security]` section of `ekos.toml` cannot disable the built-in redaction baseline. RFC 0043 defines it as a config section that "can only add to the baseline" — i.e., it can supply extra patterns, but not remove or turn off the built-in ones. The redaction implementation reinforces this: `redact` replaces every match of every built-in pattern plus every valid `config.extra_patterns` regex, and an invalid regex in `extra_patterns` is skipped silently so a config typo "must not be able to disable the built-in baseline by erroring out." The baseline (`ekos_common::redaction`) runs at every raw-content entry point regardless.

scenarios.answer: The provided CLAUDE.md excerpts only cover project status and say nothing about redaction, missed secrets, or manual allowlisting. The closest relevant claims are from RFC 0043 and `redaction.rs`: `redact` replaces every match of every built-in pattern plus every valid `config.extra_patterns` regex with `[REDACTED:<label>]`, and an invalid regex is skipped silently so a typo cannot disable the built-in baseline. RFC 0043 also describes a new `[security]` `ekos.toml` config section that “can only add to the baseline.” That additive-only design is the only config mechanism described; no claim describes a way to manually allow a specific secret through for a workspace, and no claim states what happens to a secret missed by all patterns.
